facts.text: The NCD-RisC study, led by Imperial College London with almost 800 scientists and the World Health Organization, estimated the average height of 18-year-olds born from 1896 to 1996.
The study compares people who turned 18 in 1914 with people who turned 18 in 2014.
Men in Taiwan born in 1896 averaged about 161.3 cm at age 18; men born in 1996 averaged about 174.5 cm.
Average height of men in Taiwan rose by about 13 cm (13.2 cm) between those born in 1896 and those born in 1996.
Taiwanese men born in 1896 were a little shorter than the world average (161.3 cm against 162.5 cm); those born in 1996 were taller than the world average (174.5 cm against 171.3 cm).
Japanese men born in 1976 averaged 171.4 cm, but those born in 1996 averaged slightly less, 170.8 cm.
Among men born in 1996, Taiwanese men (174.5 cm) were taller on average than Japanese men (170.8 cm), although in 1896 Japanese men (156.2 cm) were shorter than Taiwanese men.
Between those born in 1896 and those born in 1996, the average height of men rose by about 14.6 cm in Japan, 13.2 cm in Taiwan, 13.1 cm in the Netherlands, and 8.8 cm in the world as a whole.
Dutch men are the tallest men in the world, at an average of about 182.5 cm.
How tall people grow is strongly affected by nutrition and by their surroundings, not only by genes.
Within one population, differences in height between people are mostly explained by genes.
Nutrition is one of the strongest factors in how tall a population grows; long-term lack of good food can slow children's growth.
Illness in childhood can hold back growth, because a sick body has fewer nutrients left for growing.
A mother's health and nutrition during pregnancy may also affect how tall her child becomes.
In some countries, including Japan, the United States, the United Kingdom, and Finland, average height has stopped rising over the past 30 to 40 years.
In East Asian countries such as South Korea and China, average height is still rising, and their people are now taller on average than people in Japan.
Around the world, average adult height rose by roughly 8 to 10 cm over the century covered by the study.
A study found that the long rise in the height of Dutch people has come to an end in recent decades.
Dutch men born in 1976 and in 1996 both averaged about 182.5 cm.
